title.narrative: Pillar 1: Health Sector: Enhancing Nationwide Access to Secondary Healthcare for Underserved Communities (Lebanese patients, psychiatric Lebanese, migrant, and non-Syrian refugee patients)

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan id="docs-internal-guid-77f470b8-7fff-e210-f1a9-f8364f573d35" style=""gtltspan style="font-variant-numeric: normal font-variant-east-asian: normal font-variant-alternates: normal vertical-align: baseline"gtSAMS proposes to implement a nationwide health sector intervention that is aligned with LHF Standard Allocation Strategy 2023 “Pillar 1”. Hospital admissions for at least 726 patients are expected, benefitting Lebanese, non-Syrian refugee, and migrant patients in need of critical, life-saving, and psychiatric care. The proposed project will contribute to LCRP 2023 Outcome 2: Improve access to hospital (including. Emergency Room (ER) Care) and advanced referral care (including advanced diagnostic laboratory and radiology care) and Output 2.1: Financial support provided to targeted population for improved access to hospital and advanced referral care. SAMS has designed the proposed intervention after extensive consultation with UN agencies, among other key stakeholders in health, considering lessons learned after four years of experience implementing similar interventions. lt/spangtlt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp style="line-height: 1.2 margin-top: 0pt margin-bottom: 0pt" dir="ltr"gtltspan style="font-variant-numeric: normal font-variant-east-asian: normal font-variant-alternates: normal vertical-align: baseline"gtSAMS will (1) pay top-up contributions toward hospital bills of pre-approved patients for critical lifesaving care based on predetermined medical criteria that is developed by SAMS and contracted hospitals (2) provide sensitization to hospital staff on SAMS financial procedures as per auditing standards on protection and PSEA guidelines and (3) conduct patient follow-up and referrals for patients other project participants that contact SAMS.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="line-height: 1.2 margin-top: 0pt font-variant-alternates: normal vertical-align: baseline"gtVulnerable Lebanese patients of all ages, nationwide, in need of in-patient hospitalization services. Lebanese are considered amongst the most vulnerable populations in Lebanon at present because of minimal ever-decreasing coverage offered by insuring parties such as the MoPH, NSSF, COOP, due to the unfavorable LBP/USD exchange rate that these insuring parties use to calculate coverage. Of note, hospital bills are based on market USD/LBP exchange rate while ensuring parties cover at official USD/LBP exchange rate.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="line-height: 1.2 margin-top: 0pt margin-bottom: 0pt" dir="ltr"gtltspan style="font-variant-numeric: normal font-variant-east-asian: normal font-variant-alternates: normal vertical-align: baseline"gtlt/spangtltspan style="font-variant-numeric: normal font-variant-east-asian: normal font-variant-alternates: normal vertical-align: baseline"gtltspan style="white-space:pre" class="Apple-tab-span"gt lt/spangtlt/spangtltspan style="font-variant-numeric: normal font-variant-east-asian: normal font-variant-alternates: normal vertical-align: baseline"gtVulnerable psychiatric patients of all ages nationalities except Syrian patients, nationwide, in need of in-patient psychiatric services. There is little to no coverage for psychiatric admissions provided by the MoPH for Lebanese patients, no coverage for Palestinian and migrant patients. No other L/INGOs other than SAMS offer coverage to patients in need of psychiatric care. Since UNHCR is still providing coverage of psychiatric admissions for Syrian patients, this population has not been included for psychiatric coverage. It is worth noting that organizations such as Embrace, Restart, and MSF refer psychiatric patients to SAMS on a daily basis for in-patient coverage support and rely heavily on SAMS for the provision of this support. lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="line-height: 1.2 margin-top: 0pt margin-bottom: 0pt" dir="ltr"gtltspan style="font-variant-numeric: normal font-variant-east-asian: normal
